newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end mostly up at new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end mostly up at new highs.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed mostly higher with deferred contracts up at new contract highs on spread action and support generated by stronger cash ideas into the year, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.400 cent per lb lower to 0.500 higher with February off most at 64.575 cents while October through distant February posted new contract highs. Feeder cattle ended 0.175 cent lower to 1.075 higher with only January off and March up 0.175 at 69.425 cents. April through November set new contract highs.
Fund rolling kept nearby live cattle pressured.

The fund rolling of the past few sessions continued which added to resistance from slow cash trade and price weakness in boxed beef. The rolling may be finished but cash trade will have to pick up soon or nearby futures will remain pressured, they said.
"There is a lot of concern there that we don't have packers showing a lot of interest" in the cash market, said Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst for Dean Witter.
Benson noted that sliding beef prices was inhibiting packer demand for cattle.
USDA at midday quoted the price of 700- to 850-lb beef carcasses at $97.51 per cwt, well down from the week-earlier closing quote at $101.28.

But concern over death losses from recent cold weather and snow in the northern Plains and upper Midwest as well as last Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report and bullish projections for Friday's Cattle Inventory data boosted deferred months.
Early projections on the inventory report indicated total U.S. cattle numbers as of January 1 mostly down one to three percent from last year.
R.J. O'Brien and RBH sold February late while Cargill Investor Services and ADM Investor Services bought. Cargill and Shatkin sold April, pit sources said.

Spreading was active with mixed spread selling of February and buying of April and June cited along with the spread rolling. RBH bought April and sold June while LFG bought April and sold October, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, Cargill bought February 64 puts early and Refco bought June 64 calls late while also buying June, October and December futures, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures rallied from early profit taking and pressure from higher corn futures to post new contract highs in most months. Deferreds paced the advance based on the bullish ideas for the inventory report, traders said.
Most early estimates on the inventory report for feeder cattle under 500 lbs, point to a decline of one to three percent and a 1996 calf crop unchanged to two percent lower.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.41 at $69.77 per cwt.

Nearby futures pared best levels late as houses traded on both sides of the market and profit taking developed. ING, E.D.&F. Man and ADM Investor Services were on both sides. Cargill and E.D.&F. Man bought back months while RBH spread long March/short August. Refco bought October live cattle and sold May feeders while Cargill spread long October feeders/short February cattle, pit sources added.
